thread:
Priya Nair: quick brain dump from today's sync — proposal for a staggered hedging layer that lives between decision and enforcement. Purpose: avoid immediate full rollbacks, give a controlled escape path, and make ownership boundaries explicit. high level: local detector -> local gatekeeper emits candidate decision -> hedger translates to timed, probabilistic enforcement instructions -> router enforces.
Omar Haddad: sounds promising. main ask: define who can escalate from hedged -> full rollback. we need a clear escalation matrix (local owner vs global).
Kara Liu: agree. propose rule: local gatekeeper can enact soft hedges up to X% traffic for Y mins. anything beyond that requires global reconciler sign-off. default X=30%, Y=15m.
Theo Morales: also add safety budgets per-tenant. hedges consume budget; if budget exhausted, auto-escalate to full fallback or circuit-mode. budget refill rules? daily window or proportional to healthy traffic history.
Priya Nair: good call. budget model idea: tokens = healthy_request_count * safety_multiplier. tokens spend = (hedge_traffic_fraction) * time_factor. We'll sketch numbers in RFC.
Omar Haddad: implementation detail: hedger should emit enforcement instructions that are idempotent and timeboxed, e.g. `decision_id`, `step_ix`, `target_fraction`, `expires_at`. router applies only newer sequence numbers. prevents oscillation from duplicate events.
Kara Liu: add jitter to enforcement ramp to avoid thundering herd across regions. e.g. randomize ramp start within 0-30s per router instance.
ci-bot: test-run: hedger prototype ran integration test: tenant=\"beta-inc\" applied three-step hedge [70,50,20] with 10s jitter, observed stable p95 after second step. logs -> /artifacts/ci/2081124600/hedge-run.log
Theo Morales: also consider metric hygiene: hedger shouldn't depend on raw counts. use normalized signals (rates per-1000rps or percent deltas) and require at least two orthogonal signals before major escalations (latency + error rate or model-quality + drift_score).
Priya Nair: yes — require signal fusion: rule sample: `if (latency>t && error_rate>e) OR (drift>q && model_quality_drop>m)` then escalate. will include boolean policy expression in DSL.
Omar Haddad: about ownership: who owns enforcement audits? ops wants readable audit trail: `decision_id`, `issued_by`, `owner`, `contributing_signals`, `intended_effect`, `actual_effects` (post-hoc). hedger must log both planned and observed outcome.
Kara Liu: policy DSL sketch (YAML) to include `scope` (local/global), `max_soft_fraction`, `steps`, `escalation_policy`, `budget_params` and `required_signals`. e.g.
```yaml
policy:
  scope: local
  max_soft_fraction: 0.3
  steps: [0.7, 0.5, 0.2]
  step_duration_secs: 300
  escalation:
    require_global: true
    triggers: [high_drift, persistent_errors]
  budget:
    window_secs: 86400
    multiplier: 0.02
  required_signals:
    - latency_p95
    - error_rate
```
Theo Morales: for API surface: POST /signals (envelope), POST /decisions (gatekeeper -> hedger), GET /decisions/:id (audit), SSE /decisions/stream. include `schema_v`, `decision_id`, `sequence`, and `trace_id`.
Kara Liu: add `unstable_reason` free text field in decision for humans. also include `confidence_scores` array mapping to signals.
Priya Nair: testing plan: unit + integration + chaos. must simulate observer loss, signal skew (clock), partial partition where hedger can't reach router; routers must respect TTL on decisions (expire and revert to baseline). Add automated canary to ensure hedges actually reduce impact (counterfactual sampling).
Omar Haddad: ops request: expose `hedge_state` per-tenant via console and provide manual override (take-ownership button) that inserts a higher-priority `manual_decision` with `issued_by` and `expires_at`. manual decisions should preempt automated ones.
ci-bot: note: prototype enforced manual override via /decisions POST with `priority: manual` in staging. logs -> /artifacts/ci/2081124600/manual-override.log
Priya Nair: finalize next: Theo please draft the escalation matrix + budget formulas. Kara, can you shape the policy DSL and example fragments? Omar will spec idempotency and sequencing details. I'll collect and open RFC by EOD Friday.
Kara Liu: will do. also adding a small note: keep hedger light-weight and stateless where possible; store ephemeral state in Redis with TTL to keep failover cheap.
Theo Morales: +1. prefer lease-based ownership for local gatekeeper to avoid split-brain.
Priya Nair: thanks all. RFC reminder: include metrics to emit `hedge_steps_taken`, `hedge_success_rate`, `budget_consumed`, `decision_latency_ms`. ok to merge into platform RFC later.
